lessons.title: Wishes need subjunctive (quiero que…)
lessons.learn: After wishes and wants, Spanish switches mood: QUIERO QUE HABLES (I want you to speak). HABLES is SUBJUNCTIVE — for wishes, not facts. Pattern: QUIERO QUE + …ES.

grammar.title: Subjunctive after QUIERO QUE: hables
grammar.explain: QUIERO QUE + subjunctive: HABLAS (you speak, fact) → HABLES (wish). For -AR verbs: swap A→E: habla→hable, hablas→hables. Wishes live in the E-world!
mistakes: Saying QUIERO QUE HABLAS — wishes need HABLES (E, not A).
Using subjunctive for facts: VEO que hablas (fact, no switch).

dialogue.en: I want you to help me.

dialogue.t: Quiero que hables con el jefe.
dialogue.r: KYEH-roh keh AH-blehs kohn ehl HEH-feh.
dialogue.en: I want you to talk to the boss.
Agreed.

lessons.title: News and reported speech
lessons.learn: Report what others say: DICE QUE VIENE (he says he is coming). DICE QUE + normal sentence. For past reports: DIJO QUE VINO (he said he came). News verbs: INFORMAR, ANUNCIAR, CONFIRMAR.

grammar.title: Reported speech: dice/dijo que…
grammar.explain: DICE QUE + sentence (he says that…). Past: DIJO QUE + past (he said that…). The rest of the sentence stays normal — only the intro verb moves in time.
grammar.pattern: dice que + present · dijo que + past

examples.en: The paper says it is raining.

mistakes: Moving the whole sentence to past: DIJO QUE VINO (only dijo moves back).
Forgetting QUE: DICE QUE viene, with QUE!

lessons.title: Polite requests (conditional)
lessons.learn: Sound professional: ME GUSTARÍA (I would like), PODRÍA (could you…?). Conditional adds -ÍA to the whole verb: HABLARÍA, COMERÍA. ¿PODRÍA AYUDARME? = Could you help me?

grammar.title: Conditional: whole verb + ía
grammar.explain: HABLARÍA (I would speak), PODRÍA (I/he could), GUSTARÍA (would like). Same for all verbs — add -ÍA/-ÍAS/-ÍA to the infinitive. ME GUSTARÍA + verb = I would like to…
mistakes: Cutting the verb: HABLARÍA keeps -AR + ÍA.
Using QUIERO with strangers — GUSTARÍA is softer.

lessons.title: POR vs PARA (for)
lessons.learn: Two FORS! PARA = purpose/destination (PARA TI = for you, PARA MADRID = to Madrid). POR = cause/price/exchange (POR LA LLUVIA = because of rain, POR 10 EUROS = for 10 euros).

grammar.title: PARA = purpose · POR = cause
grammar.explain: PARA answers WHAT FOR / WHERE TO: ESTUDIO PARA APRENDER (I study to learn). POR answers WHY / HOW MUCH / THROUGH: POR LA MAÑANA (in the morning), POR FAVOR (please!).

examples.en: I bought it for ten euros.

mistakes: Saying POR TI for a gift — gifts are PARA ti.
Saying PARA LA LLUVIA for cause — because of = POR.

lessons.title: Idioms and sayings
lessons.learn: Idioms don't translate word-for-word! TOMAR EL PELO = to pull someone's leg (to tease). Learn them as whole chunks — they make you sound truly Spanish.

grammar.title: Idioms = whole chunks, never word-for-word
grammar.explain: COSTAR UN OJO = to cost an eye (expensive!). Translate the MEANING, not the words. Use idioms whole: ME COSTÓ UN OJO = it cost me a fortune.

examples.en: The exam was a piece of cake.
I put my foot in it yesterday.

mistakes: Translating idioms literally — learn the real meaning.
Changing idiom words: TOMAR EL PELO is fixed!

lessons.title: If-plans: si llueve, me quedo
lessons.learn: Real plans: SI + present, + present/future. SI LLUEVE, ME QUEDO (if it rains, I stay). SI VIENES, TE AYUDO (if you come, I help you). Cause meets result!

grammar.title: Real SI: si + present, + result
grammar.explain: SI LLUEVE (if it rains) → ME QUEDO (I stay). Both verbs in present, or result in future: SI VIENES, TE AYUDARÉ. Real, possible plans only!

examples.en: If you come, I help you.
If you study, you will pass.

mistakes: Using future after SI: SI LLUEVE (present!), never SI LLOVERÁ.
Forgetting the comma pause between condition and result.

dialogue.t: Si llueve, me quedo en casa.

dialogue.t: Y si hace sol, vamos a la playa.
dialogue.r: ee see AH-seh sohl, VAH-mohs ah lah PLAH-yah.
dialogue.en: And if it is sunny, we go to the beach.
Good decision!
